# Handling of the GPT pre-feasibility review report

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Original report | `review/metis-review-tien-kha-thi.md` (GPT, 02/10/2026): conclusion Go with conditions, 54 refinement requests RF-01 to RF-54 |
| Applied to | BRD version 4.2 (`brd/`), wireframes (`wireframes/`), style guide (`brand/`) |
| Directive from the product owner | A large development resource (an agency of about 40 developers). Comments based on resource limits must not change the overall picture: no cutting scope, no deferring mandatory requirements merely because of team size. Recorded as assumption A-07 in the BRD |
| How it was handled | Each finding was checked against the real documents before fixing. The findings that a machine could check were all correct: 22 mandatory requirements had no screen, MCP-10 was linked only to a V3 screen, the 1.2 → 3.2 conflict was missing a start date, "quorum 2 of 3" was placed next to "1 of 2 votes", Pass could still be clicked when mandatory artifacts were missing, the Approvals item was on the sidebar but had no screen |

Result notation: **Applied**, **Partly** (applied with adjustments), **Not applied** (with a reason), **Already covered** (the BRD already meets it).

## Findings outside the RF table

| GPT finding | Result | Reason and where it was fixed |
|---|---|---|
| The MVP scope is too large (A3 scored 2/5); proposes cutting or deferring external access, import, tree diagram, conditional flow, production Builder, MVP module, the full roadmap, allocation editor | Not applied | The reason is team size; a team of about 40 developers working in parallel can deliver the whole scope (A-07). The MVP module is already switched on or off per workspace (MVP-04); external access already depends on decision D-02 |
| Estimate of 10 to 14 FTE, 9 to 13 months | Not applied | Re-estimate in Discovery for a structure of many parallel streams (§18.2, §18.4) |
| Prototype the Builder in Discovery | Partly | Kept the Builder as a mandatory requirement; added a prototype with PMs in Discovery to reduce UX risk, without deferring it (§18.4) |
| MCP is no longer an exclusive advantage because many products already have it | Applied | Added differentiating arguments in §4.2: data derived from the WBS, versioned governance, AI going through the same permissions and the same set of metrics; the note that competitors have MCP is marked [Unverified] |
| Market evidence is needed: interviews with buyers, 1 to 2 design partners | Applied | Added to the deliverables of Discovery (§18.4), a new risk (§20) and question Q-09 |
| Five decisions to settle first | Applied | §19 adds an order: D-28, D-20, D-03, D-26 first, then D-29, D-24, D-02, D-31, D-09; D-01 updated to reflect resources |
| 30 questions for the client | Partly | Added Q-09 to Q-13 for the questions that have no corresponding decision yet; the remaining questions are already in D-01 to D-31 |
| The terms Stage and Phase are easily confused | Applied | Added "Phase" to the terminology (Appendix A) and to the in-place help PLT-20 |
